title: How long is the height QN in this parallelogram?
description: A parallelogram has a side of twelve centimetres with a height of six centimetres, and another side of seven point six centimetres. The same area is found with each base, and the second height comes from dividing.
teaching_notes: One idea: either side can be the base, so the area found with one base gives the height on the other. Watch for students who forget that the height is drawn at a right angle.

video_script.why: The child uses the area found with one base to get the height on the other base, as in the solved example.
video_script.substitution: Find the area from SR and QM, then divide it by PS.
video_script.anchor: the book's parallelogram PQRS with the heights QM and QN
video_script.payoff_line: Q N is about nine point four seven centimetres

final_answer.spoken: about nine point four seven centimetres

maths_rules: parallelogram PQRS: SR = 12 cm, QM = 6 cm, PS = 7.6 cm, QN perpendicular to PS
check: 7.6 × 9.47 = 71.97, about 72; QN < PQ = SR = 12, and QM = 6 < PS = 7.6, so the figure is possible
video_script.design: One parallelogram with two bases. The area from the first pair gives the second height.
open_questions: The answer is approximate, nine point four seven, as in the worklist.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This question is from your book.
<bookmark mark='para'/>Here is a parallelogram P Q R S. The side S R is twelve centimetres.
<bookmark mark='qm'/>The height Q M to S R is six centimetres.
<bookmark mark='ps'/>The side P S is seven point six centimetres. Q N is the height drawn to P S.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What is the length of Q N?

beats.on_screen: the parallelogram holds still and glows

marks.stop: the parallelogram glows in the accent colour

narration: <bookmark mark='stop'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: parallelogram PQRS shown twice: SR as the base with the height QM, then PS as the base with the height QN; the rule area = base × height

marks.rule: the rule area = base × height is written
marks.two: the parallelogram is shown twice, with S R as the base and then P S as the base
marks.same: an equals sign appears between the two areas

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>The area of a parallelogram is its base times its height.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Either side can be the base, if we use the height drawn to it.
<bookmark mark='same'/>Both pairs of base and height give the same area.

beats.on_screen: Given: SR = 12 cm, QM = 6 cm (height to SR), PS = 7.6 cm, QN is the height to PS

marks.given: the sides and heights are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the side S R is twelve centimetres, and its height Q M is six centimetres.
The side P S is seven point six centimetres.

marks.find: the thing to find is written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the length of the height Q N.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: take SR as the base. Area = SR × QM = 12 × 6 = 72

marks.base: S R lights up as the base with the height Q M

narration: <bookmark mark='base'/>Step one, take S R as the base, because its height Q M is given.
<bookmark mark='calc'/>Twelve times six gives the area, which is seventy two square centimetres.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: take PS as the base. The area is the same, so 7.6 × QN = 72

marks.base: P S lights up as the base with the height Q N

narration: <bookmark mark='base'/>Step two, now take P S as the base, with the height Q N.
<bookmark mark='same'/>The area is the same, so seven point six times Q N is seventy two.
<bookmark mark='div'/>Step three, divide the area by the base.
<bookmark mark='calc'/>Seventy two divided by seven point six gives about nine point four seven.

beats.on_screen: check: 7.6 × 9.47 ≈ 72; and QN is shorter than the slanting side PQ = 12

marks.len: QN is drawn shorter than PQ = 12

narration: <bookmark mark='chk'/>Step four, check it. Seven point six times nine point four seven is about seventy two.
<bookmark mark='len'/>Also Q N must be shorter than the slanting side P Q, which is twelve. It is.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Q N is about nine point four seven centimetres.
